Pozole Rojo

Mexico's celebratory hominy stew: pork simmered until tender in a brick-red guajillo broth, served with a table full of shredded cabbage, radish, oregano and lime to build your own bowl.

★★★★★★★★★★4.7(934)Rated 4.7 out of 5 from 934 reviews 3 hr total Serves 8 servings Medium Mexican
Jump to Recipe Jump to Method

Why This Recipe Works

Hominy is maize treated with an alkali, a process called nixtamalisation that releases niacin and gives the kernels their distinctive puffy chew and aroma. The broth is built in two stages — pork simmered first, chilli purée added later — so the chillies never boil long enough to turn bitter.

Method

Tap a step to highlight it, or turn on Cook Mode for large type and step-by-step focus.

  1. Put the pork shoulder and ribs in a large pot with the onion, garlic, bay and salt. Cover with 3 litres of cold water and bring slowly to a simmer, skimming the scum carefully for the first 15 minutes.

  2. Simmer gently, partly covered, for 1.5 hours until the pork is tender.

  3. Meanwhile toast the dried chillies in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side, then soak in hot water for 20 minutes.

  4. Blend the drained chillies with 300 ml of the pork broth, the oregano and cumin until completely smooth, then pass through a fine sieve.

  5. Lift the meat out, discard the aromatics and strain the broth. Shred the shoulder coarsely and pick the rib meat off the bones.

  6. Return the broth to the pot, stir in the chilli purée and simmer for 20 minutes to marry.

  7. Add the hominy and the shredded meat and simmer 20 minutes more. Taste and adjust the salt — pozole needs more than you expect.

  8. Serve in deep bowls with every garnish in its own dish, so each person builds their own.

Chef’s Tips

  • Sieving the chilli purée is essential; unsieved skins give the broth a gritty texture.
  • Dried hominy, soaked overnight and simmered for 2 hours, is superior to tinned if you can find it.
  • Pozole tastes under-seasoned until the lime and oregano go on. Season the broth, then trust the garnishes.

Pairing Suggestions

  • Mexican lager or a hibiscus agua fresca
  • The garnish plate is the side dish
  • Finish with cinnamon-dusted churros

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerate 4 days, freeze 3 months. The broth deepens overnight. Reheat gently and refresh the garnishes.
